tasks.prompt: Which colours come from mixing the primaries
tasks.explanation: Red, blue and yellow cannot be mixed from anything else, which is why they are primary. Everything else comes from them.

tasks.prompt: Build the warm side of the palette, hottest first
tasks.explanation: Warm colours recall fire and sun. They are used for whatever should feel nearer and more alive.

tasks.prompt: Lay out a landscape from far to near
tasks.explanation: Distant things are painted paler and higher, near things larger and darker. That is how flat paper gains depth.

tasks.prompt: Build the cool side of the palette
tasks.explanation: Cool colours pull the eye into the picture. That is why distant hills are painted blueish rather than brown.

tasks.prompt: Where an object is lightest and where it is darkest
tasks.explanation: A highlight and a shadow on one object make it solid. Without them a ball is just a flat circle.

tasks.prompt: Build a pair of complementary colours and what sits between
tasks.explanation: Complementary colours face each other on the wheel. Side by side they shout; mixed together they cancel out.

tasks.prompt: Compose a picture with a clear main subject
tasks.explanation: The subject goes large and near; depth comes from the far line. A shadow separates the figure from the ground.

tasks.prompt: Build a sunset in layers, from the ground up
tasks.explanation: At sunset the sky warms near the horizon and cools above. A hard edge between them gives away painting from memory.
